Venomics AI raises $2.7 Mn to discover drugs from animal venoms
The fresh capital will go towards expanding its Venom Atlas, a molecular dataset of animal venoms and hiring across biology, computational science and drug discovery.
Smruthi Nadig
ETEntrepreneur
Published On Nov 5, 2026 at 11:46 AM IST
Copy Link
Share on WhatsApp
Share on Linkedin

Share on Facebook
Venomics AI is harnessing India’s rich venom biodiversity and artificial intelligence to identify molecules with potential therapeutic applications.
Biotech startup Venomics AI has raised $2.7 million in a pre-seed round co-led by Speciale Invest and South Park Commons, with participation from Operators Studio, to advance its venom-based drug discovery platform.
The fresh capital will go towards expanding its Venom Atlas, a molecular dataset of animal venoms , strengthening its AI and laboratory screening capabilities, and hiring across biology, computational science and drug discovery.
Spun out of the Indian Institute of Science (IISC), the Bengaluru-based startup combines venom biology, AI and laboratory screening to identify molecules from animal venoms that could be developed into medicines.
“Animal venoms represent one of nature’s richest yet least explored sources of potential medicines, and at Venomics AI, we are combining cutting-edge experimental science with AI to unlock this extraordinary potential,” said Kartik Sunagar, founder and director of Venomics AI and professor at IISc.
The company, founded by Sunagar and Vinay Prabhu, combines Sunagar’s expertise in venom evolution and antivenom development with Prabhu’s background in machine learning and large-scale AI systems.
“Few people combine his deep understanding of these venoms with the access to study them. Vinay brings the AI depth to accelerate this bio-discovery,” said Arjun Rao, general partner at Speciale Invest.
The startup has established the initial architecture of its platform, joined the NVIDIA Inception programme , and been selected among the top five finalists for the 2026 Indo-Boston Biotech Bridge Award.
Prateek Mehta, general partner at South Park Commons, said, “Venom is one of nature's oldest targeting systems. It gave us Captopril and GLP-1s, and until now we've only been able to search one molecule at a time. AI changes that.”

UK Sovereign AI fund and Stripe CEO back Potential Sciences in multi-million-dollar raise
The Sovereign AI fund is providing funding and compute capacity to Potential Sciences.
John Reynolds
05 November 2026
Share
Facebook
Twitter
Linkedin
Share
Send email
Copy link
A London-based startup building AI infrastructure for scientific drug discovery has received backing from the UK government’s Sovereign AI fund and Stripe CEO Patrick Collison.
Potential Sciences leverages AI, machine learning and quantum chemistry simulations to help researchers understand how molecules behave and interact.
It is pioneering a new approach, with an AI model focused on the fundamental laws of physics, rather than previous experimental data, the startup says.
It says this could make the AI calculations needed to design chemicals 100 times cheaper than at present.
The government’s Sovereign AI fund today confirmed it was backing Potential Sciences, as part of a raise in the tens of millions of dollars. The Sovereign AI fund is also committing compute capacity to Potential Sciences, which was founded in November last year.
It marks the latest bet by the UK government's Sovereign AI fund, whose mission is to ensure that the UK develops, owns and scales key AI firms. Its other bets include chip startup Olix and AI startups Ineffable Intelligence and Callosum.
The seed funding round also includes backing from Twin Path Ventures, Odyssey, Portfolio Ventures, Blue Wire Capital, rule30, Nauta Capital and Lightfield Equity, as well as angel investment from Collison and other angel investors.
Potential Sciences declined to disclose exactly how much was raised or its valuation.
Potential Sciences was founded by doctor Hatem Helal, a former Graphcore executive, the chip designed acquired by SoftBank, in 2025.
Sovereign AI Investment Partner Joséphine Kant said: "I first met Hatem in Cambridge, and he immediately struck me as a formidable founder. He combines technical excellence with low ego and unapologetic ambition. He knows the science in extraordinary detail, but he’s also deliberate about bringing in people who are exceptional in areas different from his own.
"Potential Sciences have the ambition to become a true frontier lab for chemistry, with the potential to fundamentally change how the field works."

Funding Wrap: Clinics On Cloud, Peppermint Robotics, GIVA raise fresh capital
Here is a lowdown of this week’s top deals across deeptech, consumer brands, healthtech, and more.
ETEntrepreneur Desk
ETEntrepreneur
Published On Nov 6, 2026 at 02:21 PM IST
Copy Link
Share on WhatsApp
Share on Linkedin
Share on X
Share on Telegram
Share on Facebook
Funding Wrap This week, the funding spotlight was on deeptech, consumer brands, and healthtech startups .
ETEntrepreneur brings a roundup of key deals below.
Two Point O Capital raises $10 million led by Transition Venture Capital Two Point O Capital, an AI-powered clean energy deployment platform, has raised $10 million in a funding round led by Transition Venture Capital, with participation from existing investor Omnivore and angel investors Chiranjeev Singh Saluja and Sudhir M. Reddy.
The company will use the fresh capital to expand into new asset classes, including battery energy storage systems (BESS), while strengthening its existing offerings in solar energy, energy efficiency and wastewater treatment.
Read the whole story here .
Clinics On Cloud raises $12.5 mn series A funding from Dubai-based investors Healthtech startup Clinics On Cloud has raised $12.5 million in a series A funding round from Dubai-based investors through Model42, powered by Enlightened Minds Investments.
The company will deploy the fresh capital to strengthen its artificial intelligence-led healthcare capabilities, expand research and development, and scale its connected microclinic network.
Read the whole story here .
Upsurge India leads ₹50 crore secondary transaction in iD Fresh Food Upsurge India has led a secondary transaction worth over ₹50 crore in iD Fresh Food, involving the transfer of about 1 per cent equity in the Bengaluru-based fresh-food company.
The transaction, co-led by Triumph Global Fund and White Whale Ventures, enabled early investor Blue Ashva Capital to exit its investment.
iD Fresh Food is also working towards a potential public listing, with the company having previously indicated late 2027 as a target, subject to market conditions and its ability to strengthen profitability.
Read the whole story here .
Multiples leads over $100 mn funding in jewellery brand GIVA Multiples Alternate Asset Management has led a funding round of over $100 million, alongside its co-investors, in fine jewellery brand GIVA.
The latest funds will help the jewellery brand to strengthen its leadership team, build manufacturing capabilities, and expand its offline presence with more than 1,000 outlets over the next three to five years.
Read the whole story here .
Let’s Game Now closes ₹30 Cr funding backed by Anand Mahindra, Bestvantage Let’s Game Now, an Indian gaming and e-sports company, has closed a ₹30 crore investment round backed by industrialist Anand Mahindra and Bestvantage Investments, with a significant portion of the funding coming from a UAE-based family office.
The company plans to use the investment to accelerate the development of the Indian Super Gaming League, a franchise-based gaming league combining competitive gaming, sports, entertainment and technology.
Read the whole story here .
PowerUp Money raises $10 mn from Flourish Ventures Wealthtech platform PowerUp Money has raised $10 million in a funding round led by Flourish Ventures, with participation from existing investors Peak XV Partners, Accel, Blume Ventures, Kae Capital, 8i Ventures and DeVC.

Peppermint Robotics raises Rs 100 Cr in Pre-Series B led by pi Ventures, Crane Venture Partners
Pune-based robotics startup Peppermint Robotics has raised Rs 100 crore (around $10.5 million) in a Pre-Series B funding round led by pi Ventures and Crane Venture Partners.
Shashank Pathak
04 Nov 2026
09:49
IST
Follow Us
New Update
Pune-based robotics startup Peppermint Robotics has raised Rs 100 crore (around $10.5 million) in a Pre-Series B funding round led by pi Ventures and Crane Venture Partners. The round also saw participation from Asiana Fund.
The investment comprises a combination of primary capital and secondary share transactions.
The fresh capital will be used to expand manufacturing capacity, develop next-generation robotics solutions and strengthen the company's global operations. Peppermint also plans to establish an assembly line in North America in the coming months.
Founded in 2019, Peppermint Robotics develops autonomous robots for commercial floor cleaning and material transportation. The company has expanded its operations to nine countries, with the US emerging as its largest market.
Peppermint's robots are deployed across factories, hospitals, airports, malls, warehouses, hotels and universities. The company also serves pharmaceutical cleanrooms, where its robots have passed qualification testing in an EU GMP Grade cleanroom.
The startup develops its robotics hardware, software and perception systems in-house. Its robots use computer vision and LiDAR to map environments, plan cleaning routes and avoid obstacles. The company also offers offline robots for security-sensitive environments.
Peppermint plans to use the primary capital across five areas, including research and engineering, manufacturing expansion, North American operations, global market expansion and hiring senior leadership and engineering talent.
The company will also expand its portfolio of autonomous floor-cleaning and material-handling robots, while advancing its next-generation cleanroom robotics line.
Peppermint previously raised Rs 34 crore (around $4 million) in a Series A round in April 2025. According to the company, its revenue grew nearly sixfold between FY24 and FY26, after doubling last year.
